analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 798-1628). The changed region is at about lines 2058-2073, which is outside the supplied units. The patch excerpt is truncated at the end of the Flint paragraph. The change is documentation-only: Flint always uses native KV and native checkpoint precision, ignoring provider-wide balanced defaults. It also treats automatic paged selection for a verified FlintModel as explicit paged, and refuses the load on a contiguous selection, the paged kill switch or a capability veto.

The units I examined contain no changed lines, so no security regression can be cited from them. The surrounding text covers the following, none of which the patch alters:
- Prefix-cache, SSD and TTL behavior, relevant to T-041 and SEC-035.
- Media ingest caps.
- Deadline and calibration policy.
- MTP policy.
- Tool and reasoning parsing.

The documented Flint behavior could touch T-041 in two ways: forcing paged attention might change prefix-cache eligibility, and native-precision KV might change at-rest checkpoint format. The supplied evidence does not show whether the code actually changes the SSD or cache gates, the DBK3 crypto, HMAC naming or the TTL. The diff shown is documentation only, with no code change visible. Remaining integration questions: whether the corresponding Swift change in EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend and EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve keeps the prefix-cache identity and KV layout epoch binding unchanged for Flint, and whether refusing the load on contiguous or kill-switch selection creates any availability concern. I found no concrete finding from the supplied evidence. Because the full patch and the code are not visible, I recommend a limited deeper review of those code paths.
